chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Ray Nance's Chicago band in 1932 and Lena Horne's arrival
summary: Collins heard Nance's band at Dave's, played in Nance's big band, and once saw a beautiful Lena Horne step off Noble Sissle's bus.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Going back over the other tapes I found one -- you mentioned Ray Nance had a band in high school.
Yeah.
That was --

I didn't play with his high school band, I was in school with him. He had another guitarist, a marvelous guitarist by the name of Claude Adams. Claude died very young but Ray always had very good bands. And I played with him later in a big band, and --
Was it his big band?
It was Ray Nance's big band, yes.
His own.

Yes, yes. So we played Indianapolis, and we pulled into Indianapolis this day and Noble Sissel was -- pulled in with his bus at the same time, and out of the bus stepped this woman which was the most beautiful woman I'd ever seen in my life. It was Lena Horne. She was just gorgeous. I -- she was quite -- I think she was in her late teens then. But just beautiful.
And I played with Nance's big band. This was just an aside.
Was that when Jimmy Miller was with
(inaudible).
No, I don't believe Jimmy -- who else was with him? I did know who was with him. I don't think Jimmy was with him then. This is your friend, Jimmy.
Yes. I wasn't aware that he played with Noble Sissle. He played with Sissle, (inaudible) I don't know what time.
Yeah. Oh, I don't think he was with him. He was with him then. No, I don't think so. But any way, Nance was always a multi-talented young man. He could dance. I mean, he did everything well.
With his own band did he play trumpet and violin --
Played trumpet.
-- and sing?

And sang, yes. And had marvelous arrangements. His pianist was a kid by the name of Specs, used to call him Spencer. Jesse Simpkins was the bass player, Oliver what's that drummer, and they had a vibes, someone played vibes. But a very, very entertaining band. At this time I was working with my mother, Dan Grissom and I was working with my mother.
You said that Ray had great arrangements. Was Ray arranging or --
Well, yeah, the piano player did most of the arranging. Spencer,yeah. But I used to -- when we'd

get off of my job, Dan and I would always rush over to hear Ray. They were playing a club in Chicago, by the name of Dave's. And everybody would go there. Do you know when this was? This was 1932. Were you born then?
Thank you.
1932, yes, we'd go there to listen to Nance's band. It was very entertaining band. So Nance as I stated before is a multi-talented musician.
Were you in the same high school with Ray Nance?
Yeah.
What high school?
Wendell Phillips.
Wendell Phillips High School?
